draft.change: Retain the current personal-name article. Its Genesis 9:18 note already explains the repeated name.
draft.definition: Ham, son of Noah and father of Canaan.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 9:18, הוּא refers back to the repeated חָם and אֲבִי כְנָעַן identifies him as Canaan’s father.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan as the sons of חָם, identifying him as their father.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix. It names the father in the construct phrase וּבְנֵי חָם, “and the sons of Ham.”
analysis.sense: Ham, son of Noah and father of Canaan

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי חָם (“and the sons of Ham”) introduces a list of four sons. כּוּשׁ is the first son named.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בְנֵי חָם introduces the list of Ham’s sons. Mizraim is the second son named, between Cush and Put.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וּ means “and” and introduces the proper name מִצְרַיִם.

evidence.note: Put is the third name in the list introduced by בְנֵי חָם ‘sons of Ham’.

article.name: פּוּט
article.summary: Genesis lists Put as a son of Ham, alongside Cush, Mizraim, and Canaan. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for פּוּט with its etymology unassigned.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:6 lists Put among the sons of Ham.

analysis.evidence: בְנֵי חָם ‘sons of Ham’ introduces the list. וּפוּט names its third member, between Mizraim and Canaan. The verse identifies the bearer but gives no derivation for the name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ ‘and’ prefixes the proper name פּוּט. The initial פ appears without dagesh after the vowel of the conjunction.

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי חָם (“and the sons of Ham”) introduces a list of four names. Canaan follows Put as the last son named.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and” and introduces the proper noun כְנָעַן.
